documentBaseSemantics.name: FIRST_BASE_ELEMENT_WITH_HREF_ATTRIBUTE_IN_TREE_ORDER
documentBaseSemantics.supersedes: the earlier brief phrase "first valid <base href>", for implementation purposes
rules: find the FIRST <base> element, in document order, that HAS an href attribute (in any attribute syntax)
a <base> without an href attribute (e.g. target only) does NOT claim the document base
every later <base href> is ignored once the first href-bearing base is selected
the selected href is resolved against the fetched document URL (the fallback base)
if it does not parse, or parses to anything other than an http: or https: URL (javascript:, data:, ...), the document base is the fetched document URL
the search does NOT continue to a later <base href> after a failed first one
documentBaseSemantics.nonContent: the base is searched for only AFTER the canonical stripNonContent (src/orgunits/web/extract.ts), the same function anchor discovery already uses; a <base> inside a comment, script, style, noscript, svg, template or iframe is not seen. No second sanitiser is written.

v5BehaviouralBoundary.changes: ONLY the URL each already-extracted anchor href is resolved against: the document base instead of the fetched document URL
unchanged: admissibleUrl: root authority, registrable-domain scope, host policy, URL validation
gateway checks: SSRF/address policy, pinning, TLS, timeouts, caps
robots policy and the robots redirect continuation
request budgets 35 / 60 / 8 hosts, pacing, circuit breaker
v5BehaviouralBoundary.noBaseCompatibility: for a document with no href-bearing <base> (or whose first one falls back), the v5 frontier input is byte- and sequence-identical to v4
